name: Priced Out: simulated Columbia and Barnard undergraduates
research_objective: Find the prices at which undergraduates quietly skip a student club's dues, formal ticket or weekend trip and give a different reason for not going; which ways of offering a lower price they would actually use; and whether they would add a little to their own ticket to cover someone else. The answers feed a pricing calculator for student club treasurers. This is a simulation with AI personas and will be labelled as one wherever it is shown.
context: The personas are undergraduates at Columbia University and Barnard College in New York City: all four years, a realistic mix of majors, and a realistic mix of club involvement (some in no clubs, most in one or two, some in several, and a few who are club officers who set dues or plan paid events). Their money situations should span the real range at a selective private university with need-based financial aid. That includes students on full aid with little or no spending money who hold a work-study or part-time job, students from middle-income families who budget carefully, and students from wealthy families for whom these prices do not matter. What decides whether $30 of dues or a $60 formal ticket is easy is the student's own spending money, not the family's income. Each persona should answer as that one student honestly would, and leave a question blank when that student would.
